program_name: Master in Tourism Management. Faculty of Economics and Management, Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (unibz). level: master (Italian laurea magistrale / second-cycle degree, German Masterstudiengang). 120 ECTS over 2 years, confirmed both by the 'At a glance' box of every archived cycle ('ECTS Credits: 120, Duration of the course: 2 years') and by the official study-plan PDF, which closes with 'Total CP for graduation / CFU totali per il conseguimento del titolo: 120'. It is an ordinary second-cycle laurea magistrale, NOT a professionalising degree, NOT an executive/1st-level master (unibz runs separate 'Executive Master' and '1st Level Master' tracks, e.g. the Executive Master in Digital and Socially Sustainable Human Resources Management, which are a different animal and are still active). Structure: 60 CP taught in year 1 and 60 CP in year 2, the second year weighted towards application - a 9 CP Smart Tourism Laboratory, a 6 CP compulsory internship of at least 150 hours, and a 12 CP thesis.
teaching_language: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT NUANCE IN THE RECORD, AND THE ANSWER CHANGES BY COHORT. The programme was TRILINGUAL (German / Italian / English) for its first three intakes and ENGLISH-ONLY for its fourth and final intake. (1) Cohorts 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25: 'Courses will be taught in: German, Italian, and English (trilingual)' - verbatim from the 'At a glance' box of the archived programme page in December 2021, January 2023 and April 2024, with the matching admission rule 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' The study-plan PDF for students enrolled from 2022/23 prints every course title in all three languages (e.g. 'Managing Tourism Destination / Gestione delle Destinazioni Turistiche / Destinationsmanagement'). (2) Cohort 2025/26 - the last one: 'Courses will be taught in: English' and 'The official teaching language is English', verbatim from the archived March 2025 page. The study-plan PDF for students enrolled from 2025/26 prints course titles in ENGLISH ONLY, and the live Course Offering listing for academic year 2026/27 shows every single one of the ten scheduled course units flagged 'EN' - Data Management and Analytics, Economics of Sustainable Tourism, Thesis and Report Writing Skills, International Tourism Management Sustainability and Perspectives, Trends and Issues in Tourism Management, Culture Heritage and Creative Territory Management, Smart Tourism Laboratory, Revenue Management and Customer Profitability, Corporate Finance for Tourism Businesses and the Internship (Commercial Practice and Law in Tourism is listed without a language flag, the only gap). So in the one year in which an English-only candidate could genuinely have taken this degree from start to finish - the 2025/26 intake - the programme was 100% English, and that is precisely the year unibz stopped recruiting for it. For 2026/27 the question is academic: no one can enrol. Do not describe the programme as trilingual in a dataset aimed at applicants, and do not describe it as English-taught without stating that the English-taught version accepted exactly one cohort.
campus: Bruneck-Brunico, in the Pustertal-Pusteria valley, roughly 80 km north-east of Bolzano - NOT the Bolzano main campus, NOT NOI Techpark Bolzano and NOT Brixen-Bressanone. 'Campus: Bruneck-Brunico' appears in the 'At a glance' box of every archived cycle from 2022/23 to 2025/26. Teaching was split between the town-centre main building, Universitaetsplatz 1 / Piazzetta dell'Universita 1, 39031 Bruneck-Brunico (Faculty of Economics and Management Secretariat, +39 0474 013600, tourism@unibz.it), and NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico, Europastrasse 9 / via Europa 9, opened in 2023 on the town's former industrial area. unibz's own Master Online Info Sessions page still says lectures 'take place between the main building in the city centre and the NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico'. TWO IMPORTANT COMPLICATIONS. First, the Bruneck-Brunico campus itself is being wound down as a teaching site: on 17 April 2026 the South Tyrolean provincial government announced that university teaching moves from Bruneck to Bozen, that the sister Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management relocates to Bozen-Bolzano from 2027/28, and that Bruneck is to be strengthened as a research location - unibz's live bachelor page already warns 'Students beginning their studies in the 2026/27 academic year at the Bruneck-Brunico Campus will continue their studies at the Bozen-Bolzano Campus starting from the second year, 2027/28.' Second, salto.bz reported on the same day that 'il master era gia stato spostato a Bolzano per carenza di iscritti' (the master had already been moved to Bolzano for lack of enrolments), which conflicts with every unibz page - all of which still say Bruneck-Brunico. The most likely reading is that the surviving 2025-entry cohort is being taught out in Bolzano, but unibz has published nothing to confirm this, so treat the physical location of the remaining teach-out classes as unverified. unibz's own campus page is meanwhile stale: it still states 'In Bruneck-Brunico we offer two study programmes: the Bachelor in Tourism, Sports and Event Management and the Master in in Tourism Management' (unibz's own duplicated 'in'), advertising a programme that accepts no applications. degree_class: LM-77 - Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Sciences / Management). Verbatim from the 'At a glance' box of every cycle: 'Degree class: LM-77'; the official study-plan PDFs are headed 'Master in Tourism Management (LM-77)'. This is the general management class, NOT the tourism-specific class LM-49 (Progettazione e gestione dei sistemi turistici / Design and Management of Tourism Systems) that many Italian tourism masters use - a placement worth flagging, because LM-49 appears in this programme's own admission rules only as one of the prior qualifications that earn disciplinary bonus points, never as its own class. The class was stable for the whole life of the programme: LM-77 in the 2022/23 study plan and LM-77 in the 2025/26 study plan, with no reclassification. Practical consequence quoted on the page: 'simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-77/LM-77 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents)' - so it could not be combined with the Master in Accounting and Finance or other LM-77 programmes. The SSD codes attached to its courses were migrated to the post-2024 reform codes: the 2022/23 plan uses SECS-P/08, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/06, SECS-S/01, while the 2025/26 plan uses ECON-07/A, ECON-05/A, ECON-06/A, ECON-09/A, STAT-01/A, AGRI-01/A and GIUR-02/A for the same subject areas.

is_new_programme: No - it is a short-lived programme now closing, not a new one. FOUR INTAKES ONLY: 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26. Evidence for the 2022/23 start: the official study plan is headed 'Study plan for students enrolled starting from the a.y. 2022/2023'; the earliest Wayback capture of the programme page is 29 December 2021 and it advertises the first application window, 'Application: 01/03 - 28/04/2022'; the internal Course Offering path is still /course-offering-2022/, later relabelled 'Course Offering - Enrolled before 2025'; and no earlier snapshot, manifesto or predecessor programme could be found. LIFECYCLE, which reads as a failed rescue: launched 2022/23 as a trilingual German/Italian/English master at about EUR 1,350 a year with a viability clause requiring at least 15 new enrolments; run unchanged for 2023/24 and 2024/25; then, for 2025/26, given a second, English-only study plan ('Study plan for students enrolled starting from the a.y. 2025/2026'), a rewritten curriculum, a single English B2 entry requirement, a fee cut to about EUR 1,200, and - notably - the removal of the minimum-enrolment clause from the page; and then suspended after that single English cohort. The 2025/26 relaunch therefore lasted exactly one intake. Two related programmes should not be confused with it: the sister Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management (L-18, trilingual, 100 EU + 4 non-EU places), which is still recruiting for 2026/27 and moves to Bozen-Bolzano from 2027/28, and the Executive Master in Digital and Socially Sustainable Human Resources Management, a different level of qualification.
majors_tracks_study_plans: NO MAJORS, NO TRACKS AND NO DUAL-STUDY VARIANT - a single 120 CP path with a few internal choices. What does exist is TWO GENERATIONS OF STUDY PLAN, and this matters because they differ in language and in content. PLAN A - 'students enrolled starting from the a.y. 2022/2023' (trilingual cohorts 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25; course codes 31000-31026; old SSD codes SECS-P/02, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/08, SECS-S/01). PLAN B - 'students enrolled starting from the a.y. 2025/2026' (the single English-only cohort; new SSD codes ECON-05/A, ECON-06/A, ECON-07/A, ECON-09/A, STAT-01/A, AGRI-01/A, GIUR-02/A). PLAN B IN FULL, from the live study-plan page. Year 1 (54 CP): Destination Management 6; Experiential Tourism Marketing 6; Research Methods and Experimental Design 6; then a compulsory choice of one 12 CP block - either 'Regional Development and Sustainability' (Regional Economics and Development 6 + Sustainable Mobility 6) or 'Regional Development and New Digital Economy' (Regional Economics and Development 6 + Digital Economics 6), with unibz's own footnote 'Students have to choose between Regional Development and Sustainability or Regional Development and Digitalisation' (note the third naming variant for the same block); Leadership and Human Resource Management in Tourism 6; Technological Trends and Applications in Tourism 6; Free Choice 12. Year 2 (66 CP): Smart Tourism Laboratory 9; Thesis and Report Writing Skills 3, marked '*propedeutical for the conclusion of the final Thesis'; Revenue Management and Corporate Finance in Tourism 12 (Revenue Management and Customer Profitability 6 + Corporate Finance for Tourism Businesses 6); Data Management and Analytics 6; ONE complementary subject from International Tourism Management Sustainability and Perspectives 6 or Economics of Sustainable Tourism 6; ONE typical subject from Trends and Issues in Tourism Management 6 or Culture Heritage and Creative Territory Management 6; Commercial Practice and Law in Tourism 6; Internship 6; Thesis 12. The internship is compulsory and quantified: 'we are part of a large network of collaboration with employers in Italy and abroad where you can undertake your compulsory internship of a minimum of 150 hours'. Plan A had the same skeleton but different labels, including 'Regional Development and Digitalization' as the alternative 12 CP block and 12 CP typical-subject choices rather than the later 6 + 6 split.
english_only_accessibility: For 2026/27: CLOSED OUTRIGHT - no application route exists for any candidate, English-speaking or otherwise, so this programme must be shown as unavailable. For the record, and this is the sharp irony of the case, in its final cycle it was one of the MOST open programmes at unibz for an English-only applicant: status 'open'. The 2025/26 rules required exactly one language, at a modest level - 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2' - with NO second language, NO third language, NO B1 threshold for sitting exams and, critically, NO EXIT LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT published at all, so a graduating student faced no German or Italian hurdle. Every course in the final study plan is delivered in English. An English-only Turkish applicant with a suitable bachelor could therefore have applied, been ranked, enrolled and graduated in English, and would even have earned 3 selection points for holding C1 English. That door was open for one admissions cycle and is now shut. In the trilingual years 2022/23-2024/25 the same programme was effectively closed to an English-only candidate: entry demanded C1 in a first language plus B2 in a second, chosen from German, Italian and English, so English alone filled only one of two mandatory slots; graduation demanded C1 / C1 / B1 across all three; and B1 in the third language was needed merely to sit exams taught in it. Practical guidance for an English-only candidate today: this record exists to stop them applying. The closest still-recruiting unibz alternatives in the same faculty are the Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management, the Master in Accounting and Finance and the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance - none of them tourism-specific - while the sister Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management remains trilingual and therefore is NOT an English-only option.
admission_type: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 - there is no admission procedure, no application window, no ranking list and no quota, because the programme is not activated. HISTORICAL REGIME, in force unchanged from the first intake to the last: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numerus clausus) decided by a DOCUMENTS-ONLY selection. There was no entrance examination of any kind, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE requirement, no portfolio, no video, no motivation letter and no interview - the Admission Committee simply scored the file. Verbatim: 'The selection procedure involves the following evaluation criteria: a) Average marks (max. 80 points) ... b) Additional language skills ... c) Disciplinary skills'. A language pre-check acted as a hard filter before scoring ('otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'), as did a legible identity document ('if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'). This makes it one of the lowest-friction admission processes at unibz - a fact worth recording precisely because the programme still failed to fill and was suspended.
academic_requirements: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 (no intake). Requirements as published for the final 2025/26 intake, which were identical in substance across all four cycles. TWO ROUTES. ROUTE 1 - a bachelor degree in one of these Italian degree classes, or an equivalent qualification gained abroad or in Italy under previous regulations: L-14 Legal services; L-15 Tourism; L-16 Administration; L-18 Economics and Business Administration; L-33 Economics; L-36 Political sciences and international relations; L-41 Statistics. Footnote: 'Italian citizen who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.' ROUTE 2 - 'a Bachelor in a different degree class to the ones listed above or an equivalent qualification gained abroad. At least 6 credit points must have been acquired in one or more of these subject areas: Business Administration, Economics, Statistics.' That 6 CFU curricular minimum is the single make-or-break number for a candidate from an unrelated field, and unibz published the exhaustive list of qualifying scientific-disciplinary sectors in BOTH the post-2024-reform codes and their pre-reform equivalents: ECON-01/A (ex SECS-P/01) Economics; ECON-02/A (ex SECS-P/02) Economic Policy; ECON-03/A (ex SECS-P/03) Public Economics; STEC-01/A (ex SECS-P/04) History of Economic Thought; ECON-05/A (ex SECS-P/05) Econometrics; ECON-04/A (ex SECS-P/06) Applied Economics; ECON-06/A (ex SECS-P/07) Business administration, Accounting and Performance Measurement; ECON-07/A (ex SECS-P/08) Management; ECON-09/A (ex SECS-P/09) Finance; ECON-08/A (ex SECS-P/10) Organization Studies; ECON-09/B (ex SECS-P/11) Financial Markets and Institutions; STEC-01/B (ex SECS-P/12) Economic History; ECON-10/A (ex SECS-P/13) Commodity Sciences; STAT-01/A (ex SECS-S/01) Statistics; STAT-01/B (ex SECS-S/02) Statistics for experimental and technological research; STAT-02/A (ex SECS-S/03) Economic statistics; STAT-03/A (ex SECS-S/04) Demography; STAT-03/B (ex SECS-S/05) Social statistics; STAT-04/A (ex SECS-S/06) Mathematical Methods for Economy, Finance and Actuarial Sciences; IEGE-01/A (ex ING-IND/35) Business and management engineering. TWO ANTI-GAMING RULES that a careless reader would miss: 'Courses included in the Master of Science in Tourism and Management course syllabus are not valid for the acquisition of the 6 CFU required as a curricular requisite for admission' (note unibz's own garbled rendering of its programme name), and 'Courses considered valid for the acquisition of the aforementioned 6 CFUs may not be used to shorten one's career' - i.e. the credits used to qualify cannot later be recycled as exemptions. A foreign bachelor also had to evidence at least 180 ECTS and give access to a master programme in the home system. National rule: 'simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-77/LM-77 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents).'
entry_exam_or_test: NONE - IN ANY CYCLE, AND NONE FOR 2026/27. This programme never used an entrance examination. There was no unibz-run admission test, no TOLC-I or TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no GMAT or GRE requirement and no subject test; admission rested entirely on the documentary score described in selection_scoring. The only examinations ever connected to the application were LANGUAGE proficiency exams run by the unibz Language Centre, which are a way of proving a language level rather than a selection test, and which candidates could book through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams'. Their dates for the final 2025/26 intake were: 2025-03-17 (registration 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-09) and 16, 17, 22 and 23 April 2025 (registration 2025-03-24 to 2025-04-08) for the Early Bird window; 2025-06-23 to 2025-06-27 (registration 2025-05-28 to 2025-06-15) for the Late window. For the 2024/25 cycle the equivalent dates were 2024-03-18 (registration 2024-03-01 to 2024-03-10), 17, 18, 19, 22 and 23 April 2024 (registration 2024-03-25 to 2024-04-09), and 24 to 29 June 2024 (registration 2024-05-29 to 2024-06-16). Note that unibz's Language Centre can only certify at B2 - 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams' - which was exactly the entry level required in the final English-only cycle, so this route was sufficient for admission but could not deliver the C1 that earned the 3 bonus points. No exam of any kind is scheduled for 2026/27 on this programme.
selection_scoring: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27. The rubric published for the final 2025/26 intake, verbatim under 'Admission procedure - The selection procedure involves the following evaluation criteria': (a) AVERAGE MARKS, max. 80 points - 'University degree: the final university grade expressed in thirtieths. University degree not obtained: the average university grade expressed in thirtieths. In the case of a degree awarded with top marks and "cum laude", an additional 2 points will be awarded.' (b) ADDITIONAL LANGUAGE SKILLS - 'You will receive 3 points if you demonstrate at least a C1 level in the official language of the course (English). Certificates recognised by the Language Centre as well as language exams taken at the Language Centre of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano will be assessed.' (c) DISCIPLINARY SKILLS, up to 15 points - awarded to candidates who hold, or are completing, a degree in L-18 Economics and Business Management Sciences, L-33 Economics or L-15 Tourism Sciences under D.M. 270/04; classes 17, 28 or 39 under D.M. 509/99; LM-77 Economics and Business Sciences, LM-56 Economics or LM-49 Design and Management of Tourism Systems under D.M. 270/04; 84/S, 64/S or 55/S under D.M. 509/99; or a pre-D.M.-509/99 qualification deemed equivalent, or a foreign qualification recognised as suitable. The components therefore cap at 80 + 3 + 15 = 98, rising to 100 with the cum laude bonus. TIE-BREAK, published: 'In the event of a tied score, as provided for in art. 26 paragraph 2, letter b) of the admission regulations in force, priority will be given to candidates who have obtained a higher partial score in the preponderant evaluation criterion in determining the overall ranking score. In the event of a further tie, priority will be given to the youngest candidate.' NO MINIMUM PASS MARK, NO CUT-OFF SCORE AND NO MINIMUM GRADE AVERAGE were ever published for this programme - unlike the Master in Software Engineering (24/30) or the Master in Energy Engineering (22/30) - and because the 2025/26 ranking lists have been deleted from the live site, no admitted-score floor can be reported either. HOW THE RUBRIC DRIFTED, which is itself informative: in the 2022/23 cycle criterion (b) read 'Aspiring students are awarded 5 points if they certify knowledge of a third language at level B2'; from 2023/24 the same clause was cut to 3 points; and for the English-only 2025/26 cycle it was rewritten from a third-language reward into an English-C1 reward - the clearest single trace of the programme's conversion to English. [uncertain]
bonus_points: Three additive components existed, all inside the selection rubric rather than as separate bonuses, and all now moot. (1) CUM LAUDE: 'In the case of a degree awarded with top marks and "cum laude", an additional 2 points will be awarded' - the only way to exceed 98 and reach a full 100. (2) LANGUAGE: 3 points for certified C1 in English in the final cycle, assessed only through 'Certificates recognised by the Language Centre as well as language exams taken at the Language Centre of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano'; in the trilingual years the same slot rewarded a THIRD language at B2, worth 5 points in 2022/23 and 3 points from 2023/24. Note the practical trap for an English-only candidate in the final cycle: the unibz Language Centre could only examine at B2, so the 3 C1 points were reachable only with an external recognised certificate. (3) DISCIPLINARY BACKGROUND: up to 15 points for a prior degree in an economics, management or tourism class (L-18, L-33, L-15, LM-77, LM-56, LM-49 and their pre-reform equivalents), which is the largest discretionary block and effectively rewarded candidates coming from the sister Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management. WHAT DID NOT APPLY: no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that belongs to the Master in Software Engineering and the Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation), no bonus for work experience in tourism or hospitality, and no bonus for South Tyrolean residence. The internal weighting within the 15-point disciplinary block was never published - unibz stated only the maximum - so it is not knowable how a tourism bachelor scored against an economics bachelor.
portfolio_and_materials: NONE REQUIRED - no portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters, in any cycle. The format limits published for the creative programmes (portfolio max 20 MB PDF, project proposal max 2 A4 pages, motivation letter max 6,000 characters, video max 2 minutes) never applied here, and neither did the research-proposal requirements of the PhD calls. The upload burden was purely evidentiary: a legible identity document; the degree documentation (diploma supplement or self-declaration if graduated in Italy, diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed if graduated abroad, transcript of records if not yet graduated), which had to show 'final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)' plus, for foreign qualifications, the 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'; a MANDATORY STRUCTURED EXCEL FILE for candidates who had not yet graduated - 'If you have not graduated yet, you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal'; and optional language certificates for the 3 bonus points. unibz also reserved a discretionary power: 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary' - relevant to Route 2 candidates proving their 6 CFU. For 2026/27 nothing can be submitted at all.
interview: NO INTERVIEW, IN ANY CYCLE. Selection was decided entirely on the documentary score, and no interview dates were ever published for this programme, in contrast with the Master in Computing for Data Science, which schedules interviews for candidates below its threshold. The governing sentence is 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline' - a closed-file procedure with no oral stage and no opportunity to supplement after the deadline. The only live conversations unibz offered were voluntary and promotional: an Online Info Session on Monday 24 March 2025 at 18:00 CET during the final recruitment round, plus Advisory Service appointments and, on request by e-mail, a campus tour of Bruneck-Brunico. For 2026/27 the question is moot - there is no selection process to be interviewed for, and the programme is absent from the 2026/27 Master Online Info Sessions.
conditional_admission: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27. Historical rule, stable across all four cycles and notably generous by unibz standards. THRESHOLD: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: You can apply if you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS). In this case, you will be admitted conditionally, and you need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The 140 ECTS figure is higher than the 120 ECTS used by most unibz masters and matches the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management; a candidate on a 180 ECTS bachelor therefore needed to be roughly five-sixths of the way through. PROOF: the structured Excel template in the application portal was compulsory for this route. CONSEQUENCE OF LATE GRADUATION, stated twice on the page and worth quoting in full because it contains actionable financial advice: 'If you graduate after the enrolment deadline: You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list. In this case. you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you can enrol by 12 December 2025.' (unibz's own punctuation error preserved.) That late-enrolment backstop moved every year: 17 December 2021 and 16 December 2022 in the first cycle's page, 15 December 2023, 13 December 2024, and 12 December 2025 in the final cycle. SEPARATE AND HARSHER RULE for the qualification itself: 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents' and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Refunds were available only in two situations - failing the final examination of the previous qualification, or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, failing to obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE - and not merely because the programme is suspended. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) is a first-cycle instrument in the Italian system, assigned to bachelor entrants whose prior knowledge is judged inadequate; at unibz it attaches to the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management through a compulsory mathematics test, and to some engineering and agriculture bachelors through the entrance exam. Master programmes at unibz do not assign OFA: the equivalent gatekeeping happens up front, through the curricular prerequisite (a qualifying degree class, or any bachelor plus at least 6 CFU in Business Administration, Economics or Statistics) and through the 140 ECTS conditional-admission floor. No OFA, no integrative credits, no bridging semester and no pre-enrolment remediation were ever published for this master in any of its four cycles. The nearest thing to remedial provision was the optional preparatory-course window before the first semester - for the 2025/26 cohort 'Preparatory courses (optional): 22/09 - 03/10/2025', and in 2024/25 a 'Mathematics pre-course: 23/09 - 04/10/2024' - which was voluntary and carried no consequence for progression. No OFA can be assigned in 2026/27 in any case, since there is no intake.
language_requirements: TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT REGIMES, split by cohort - conflating them is the single easiest way to get this programme wrong. FINAL 2025/26 INTAKE (English-only): 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' That is the entire requirement. There is NO second language, NO third language, NO B1 threshold for sitting exams, and NO EXIT LEVEL published anywhere on the page - the 'Exit level (to graduate)' block that appeared in every trilingual cycle was deleted along with the trilingual regime, so a student in the final cohort has no language hurdle standing between them and graduation. TRILINGUAL INTAKES 2022/23, 2023/24 AND 2024/25: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) 1st language: C1, 2nd language: B2, 3rd language: no level required. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Exit level (to graduate) 1st language: C1, 2nd language: C1, 3rd language: B1.' Position rather than identity fixed the level - 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner)' - and certification was 'mandatory for the first and second language, for the third language it is recommended (from B1 onwards)'. Free Language Centre courses supported the third language, 'aim[ing] to help the students reach the level B1 in the third language after the first study year'. Note the asymmetry with the sister Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management, which remains trilingual: the master's C1 first-language bar was one notch above the B2/B2 pattern used by several unibz bachelors, making the trilingual master harder to enter linguistically than the bachelor that feeds it.
entry_levels_by_position: FINAL 2025/26 INTAKE: a single position - English B2. There is no 2nd- or 3rd-language slot at all, which puts this programme in the small group of genuinely monolingual unibz degrees and, at B2 rather than C1, at the lower of the two English bars used by unibz masters (compare C1/B2 at the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance and the Master in Accounting and Finance). TRILINGUAL INTAKES 2022/23-2024/25: 1st language C1 / 2nd language B2 / 3rd language no level required at entry, with the languages drawn from German, Italian and English and assigned by the candidate to the three slots according to what they could certify. Two operational riders applied in those years: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language', and certification was compulsory for slots one and two but only recommended from B1 upwards for slot three. Because unibz's Language Centre 'can only register for B2 level exams', the C1 first-language slot always had to be filled by high-school or degree medium of instruction, or by an external recognised certificate - the Language Centre route alone could never satisfy it. For 2026/27 these levels are inoperative for admission, no candidate being admissible; the surviving 2025-entry cohort is governed by the English-only regime, which imposes nothing further.
exit_levels: FINAL 2025/26 INTAKE: NONE PUBLISHED. The archived March 2025 page carries an 'Entry level (to gain admission)' block and no 'Exit level (to graduate)' block, so a student admitted into the English-only cohort - the only cohort still being taught - faces no certified language level as a condition of graduation. This is the decisive practical difference between this programme and every trilingual unibz degree, and it is the reason the final cycle was genuinely completable in English. TRILINGUAL INTAKES 2022/23-2024/25: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B1. A student admitted at C1/B2 therefore had to raise the second language a full level and additionally reach B1 in a third, all within two years, on top of a curriculum that already carried a 150-hour internship and a 12 CP thesis. Note that the trilingual master's B1 exit level in the third language was one notch BELOW the B2 demanded by unibz's trilingual bachelors, a concession consistent with the shorter two-year span. Since the Course Offering shows no courses at all for the pre-2025 cohorts in 2026/27, any student still finishing under the trilingual regime is doing so on residual exams and the thesis, and remains bound by C1/C1/B1. third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE to the final English-only cohort - with one official teaching language there is no third language and no such threshold, and the sentence does not appear on the 2025/26 page. It applied in full to the trilingual cohorts 2022/23-2024/25, verbatim: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' Under that regime the rule had real teeth, because the trilingual study plan distributed compulsory courses across German, Italian and English, so a student who could not certify B1 in their weakest language was locked out of the exams delivered in it. unibz supported the requirement with free Language Centre provision explicitly targeted at it - 'The language courses offered by the Language Centre are free of charge and aim to help the students reach the level B1 in the third language after the first study year' - and with a placement test after admission for students who could not certify. The general unibz rider also applied: a student whose first semester is taught only in English and whose third language is English must certify B1 English by mid-January to sit that semester's exams. None of this constrains the 2025-entry cohort now being taught out.
proof_pathways: NOT APPLICABLE FOR 2026/27 for admission purposes, since no application can be created; the routes are recorded because they are the exact mechanism a comparable unibz application uses and because the deadline structure is the part applicants most often get wrong. certificate_rules: The university-wide unibz regime applied; nothing programme-specific was ever published for this master, and since the admission-information PDF is now an empty shell in all three languages there is no programme-level source left to cite. Governing instrument, verified by direct download on 2026-08-29: 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026)' / 'Beschluss des Universitaetsrates Nr. 16/2026' / 'Delibera del Consiglio dell'Universita n. 16/2026', published at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf . Core rules: a certificate must assess all four skills and be issued by the certification provider itself, and must show adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade or through faithful detailed documentation; where no overall level is shown, THE LOWEST SUB-SKILL LEVEL DETERMINES the certified level, provided that component was passed; there is no compensation for failed components and no averaging unless the awarding body itself provides it; certificates assembling single skills from different organisations are refused; certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, exams from private education providers and placement-test results are refused; certificates issued by individual lecturers, readers or teachers are refused; DAAD certificates are expressly not recognised; and remote 'home edition' exams are not recognised except for the specific entries footnoted as such in the list. VALIDITY: an international language certificate must have been obtained within the five years preceding submission, with the whole calendar year counting from 1 January. For the final English-only cycle only English mattered, so the practical set was the recognised English boards (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL, LanguageCert, Trinity and the others listed) at B2 or above; unibz's own 2026/27 Additional Application Session page even signposts LanguageCert as the fallback when no Language Centre exam is available, which is a useful indication of what it treats as reliable. This paragraph reproduces the university-wide regime rather than a source verified against this suspended programme. [uncertain]

parity_of_treatment: The standard unibz rule applied throughout the programme's life and is recorded for completeness even though no application route now exists. TWO CATEGORIES were treated as EU citizens. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' CRITICAL WARNING, in unibz's own words: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The second category was the decisive one for Turkish nationals already living in Italy on a work, family or humanitarian permit: it opened the 28-place EU pool and both EU sessions instead of the 2-place non-EU quota, removed the EUR 50 application fee, and bypassed the Universitaly and visa chain entirely. Note the wording drift across cycles - the 2022/23 and 2023/24 pages carried a truncated sentence, 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not.', which unibz later completed to '... is not valid.' application_fee: NO FEE IS PAYABLE FOR 2026/27 because no application can be made. Application fee: EUR 50.' The charge fell only on non-EU citizens living abroad, was an administration fee and was non-refundable. scholarships_grants: No scholarship specific to this master was ever published, and for 2026/27 the point is moot for new applicants since none can enrol; the general provincial regime remains relevant only to the students finishing the degree. Principal instrument: the study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Amt fuer Hochschulfoerderung / Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario, awarded on income and merit, quoted by unibz at between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year, with holders additionally receiving a refund of tuition fees - the programme page confirms the refund limb directly: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' Three provincial instruments exist (ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants fostering postgraduate studies), applied for through the provincial e-government service. Merit route: students achieving an average of 27/30 after the first year may apply on merit rather than income. DECISIVE RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: a non-EU student can apply for a provincial study grant only with a long-term residence permit or after at least one uninterrupted year of residence in South Tyrol, so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa was effectively excluded in year one - which, on a two-year master, means half the degree. Foreign students and Italian students living abroad may also apply for scholarships funded by the Ministero degli Affari Esteri, and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship are exempt from unibz fees outright. One programme-linked financial feature stands in place of a scholarship: the compulsory internship of at least 150 hours, served through unibz's network of tourism employers in Italy and abroad, which in practice often carried an allowance - but that is a placement arrangement, not a grant. These figures come from unibz's general applicant pages and were not re-verified against a programme-specific source, the programme-specific source having been emptied. [uncertain]
credential_recognition: The standard unibz foreign-qualification regime applied while the programme recruited; it now matters only to enrolled students. At enrolment, a holder of a foreign university degree had to upload: the bachelor degree diploma; an 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; and the 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. Then, by education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein - the Statement of Correspondence from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention - a Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification (https://cimea-diplome.it/). NOTE A DEFECT IN UNIBZ'S OWN TEXT: under (c) the page says the Statement of Comparability is 'to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database - Italy', whereas ARDI issues Statements of Correspondence and CIMEA issues Statements of Comparability; the 2022/23 version of the page instead said only 'In case of doubt, unibz reserves the right to request the Statement of comparability'. Applicants should assume CIMEA. FOR A TURKISH CANDIDATE: Turkey is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so category (b) applied - ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification, with an official Italian translation of a Turkish-language diploma and transcript, and a diploma supplement or equivalent evidencing at least 180 ECTS and access to second-cycle study. unibz reserved verification powers throughout: 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents' and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Separately, and now the more useful provision for anyone caught by the suspension: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz. You can fill out the application after enrolment.'

uncertainty_notes: 1) HEADLINE, AND THE POINT OF THIS RECORD: the programme is NOT available for 2026/27 and must be surfaced to users as unavailable. unibz states it explicitly, and seven independent signals corroborate it - the notice itself, the deleted 'Application and Admission' section, the deleted 'At a glance' box, the empty admission PDF in EN/DE/IT, the gutted brochure, absence from every 2026/27 ranking list, and absence from the 2026/27 Additional Application Session. Confidence: very high. 2) THIS LOOKS LIKE PERMANENT DISCONTINUATION, NOT A PAUSE - and that is a stronger claim than could be made about the other suspended unibz programme. unibz's own wording is year-specific ('will not be offered in the 2026/27 academic year') and it has published no decree, news item or press release announcing or explaining the decision. But the surrounding facts point one way: on 17 April 2026 the South Tyrolean provincial government decided that university TEACHING leaves Bruneck-Brunico for Bozen and that Bruneck becomes a research location; the sister bachelor relocates to Bozen from 2027/28; unibz's Course Offering schedules the last teaching for this master in 2026/27 and shows an empty 2027/28; and salto.bz reports the master was already moved for lack of enrolments. Recommended label: 'not offered in 2026/27, no announced return, campus being wound down as a teaching site'. Do not state flatly that it is abolished - unibz has not said so. 3) WHY IT CLOSED, as far as the record supports: chronic under-recruitment. The programme carried an explicit viability floor of 15 new enrolments in three of its four cycles; it needed a third, Super Late ranking round published 10 October 2025 - after teaching had begun - to fill its final cohort; and provincial figures put the whole Bruneck student body at about 240, down nearly a third in ten years. Actual enrolment numbers for this master are NOT published and could not be recovered. 4) LAST INTAKE was 2025/26, established from the archived programme page (a complete admission section with 2025 dates), from the brochure cover '2025/26', from the study plan 'for students enrolled starting from the a.y. 2025/2026', and from the 2026/27 course offering containing only second-year subjects. FIRST INTAKE was 2022/23, established from the study plan 'from the a.y. 2022/2023', the December 2021 page advertising the March-April 2022 window, and the absence of any earlier snapshot - four intakes in total. 5) THE LANGUAGE HISTORY IS THE BIGGEST TRAP IN THIS RECORD. Search engines, aggregator sites and cached copies of the brochure still describe this as a TRILINGUAL master at EUR 1,350 per year, because that was true for 2022/23-2024/25. It was ENGLISH-ONLY at about EUR 1,200 for its final 2025/26 intake. Both statements are true of different cohorts and neither is true of 2026/27. Anything presented to an English-speaking applicant must be dated. 6) CAMPUS CONFLICT, unresolved: every unibz page says Bruneck-Brunico; salto.bz says the master had already been moved to Bolzano for lack of enrolments. The likeliest reconciliation is that the teach-out classes are held in Bolzano while unibz's static pages were never updated, but no unibz source confirms this and the timetable was not checked. 7) SCRAPER TRAPS, several and severe. The programme is still listed in the Faculty of Economics and Management navigation menu among active programmes; it is still listed on unibz's general Course Offering index; the Bruneck-Brunico campus page still names it as one of two programmes taught there; the Master Online Info Sessions page still describes it as based at Bruneck-Brunico; and the admission-information and brochure PDFs still return HTTP 200. Any pipeline keying on menu presence, index presence, PDF existence or HTTP status will misclassify this programme as open. The reliable machine-readable signals are the empty admission PDF, the missing 'Application and Admission' and 'At a glance' blocks, and absence from the ranking-list index and the Additional Application Session page. A further, subtler trap: because the live page no longer LINKS to the study plan or course offering, a crawler that follows links will conclude those pages do not exist, yet both still resolve by direct URL and both contain current data. 8) SEARCH-ENGINE SNIPPETS FOR THE BROCHURE URL ARE STALE. Queries still return 'Master in Tourism Management 2025/26 At a glance Degree class: LM-77' with places, trilingual teaching and EUR 1,350 against the brochure PDF path; the file at that path today contains none of that. Do not scrape snippets as content. 9) NO RANKING LIST SURVIVES from any cycle - unibz keeps only the current year online and the 2025 PDFs now 404 - so there is no admitted-score floor, no applicant count and no exclusion count, and no evidence that either of the 2 non-EU places was ever taken. The selection rubric was published only as component maxima (80 + 3 + 15, plus 2 for cum laude); no pass mark, cut-off or internal weighting of the 15-point disciplinary block was ever published. 10) NO STUDY MANIFESTO OR PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC REGULATION could be located in any language, so the founding parameters of the programme are reconstructed from the earliest archived page rather than from a legal instrument, and no instrument formalising the suspension was found. 11) THE GERMAN AND ITALIAN NAMES are only partly attested. The Italian 'Laurea magistrale in Management del Turismo' is still indexed against the Italian URL from the trilingual era; no single official German programme name was confirmed, only German course titles inside the trilingual study plan. All four current language versions serve the English name. 12) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES IN UNIBZ'S OWN TEXT, recorded so they are not mistaken for research errors: the same 12 CP block is called 'Regional Development and New Digital Economy' in the study plan body, 'Regional Development and Digitalisation' in its footnote and 'Regional Development and Digitalization' in the 2022/23 plan; the entry requirements refer to a 'Master of Science in Tourism and Management'; the credential rules attribute the Statement of Comparability to ARDI rather than CIMEA; the student representative differs between the live page, the brochure and the archived page; and the 2022/23 and 2023/24 pages carry the truncated sentence 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not.' 13) CERTIFICATE RULES AND SCHOLARSHIP FIGURES reproduced here are university-wide and were not re-verified against a programme-specific source, the programme-specific source having been emptied. 14) EXIT LANGUAGE LEVELS for the final cohort are recorded as 'none published', which is an argument from absence: the 'Exit level (to graduate)' block simply does not appear on the 2025/26 page, as is normal for unibz's English-only masters, but no positive statement confirming there is no graduation language requirement was found.
